plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the StyleGAN architecture, organized into three labeled vertical columns: the main generative pipeline (center), the noise injection branch (left of center), and the style branch (right). In the style branch, a latent variable z (1×1×512) is passed through a fully connected network to produce an intermediate variable w (1×1×512), which then feeds three separate linear transforms (each outputting 2×1×512) to generate style vectors y₁, y₂, y₃ that apply per-channel scale and offset adjustments at successive resolution levels of the generator. The main generative pipeline begins with a learned constant input (4×4×512) and passes through convolutional blocks that double in spatial resolution from 4×4×512 to 8×8×512, with each block receiving the corresponding style injection. The noise branch contributes three additive perturbations (z₁⊗ψ₁, z₂⊗ψ₂, z₃⊗ψ₃) from thin 4×4×1 or 8×8×1 noise volumes, each scaled and broadcast across all channels to introduce stochastic spatial variation at different resolutions. Underbrace labels at the bottom group the three columns under the headings Main generative pipeline, Noise, and Style. This figure demonstrates how StyleGAN separates high-level content from fine-grained stochastic detail by injecting global style information through adaptive normalization and local noise directly into the feature maps at each scale.

elements: Row label brace + text 'Noise' (top-left)
Row label brace + text 'Main generative pipeline' (middle-left)
Row label brace + text 'Style' (bottom-left)
Grey learned-constant block 4×4×512 (start of main pipeline)
Thin rounded cyan slab (noise addition) after grey block
Thin rounded dark-slate slab (AdaIN style modulation) after the cyan slab
Orange convolution block 4×4×512 (second main block)
Second thin cyan noise slab + second dark-slate AdaIN slab
Large orange convolution block 8×8×512 (upsampled)
Third (tall) thin cyan noise slab + third tall dark-slate AdaIN slab
Final large orange convolution block 8×8×512
Output RGB image plane (pixelated brown/tan patchwork) at far right
Thin cyan noise plane 4×4×1 labelled 'Noise z1 ⊗ ψ1'
Thin cyan noise plane 4×4×1 labelled 'Noise z2 ⊗ ψ2'
Taller thin cyan noise plane 8×8×1 labelled 'Noise z3 ⊗ ψ3'
Three downward pale arrows from noise planes into the cyan slabs
Caption 'Noise added to every channel' beside first noise arrow
Blue-grey latent bar 1×1×512 labelled 'Latent variable z'
Orange intermediate bar 1×1×512 labelled 'Intermediate variable w'
Short arrow + label 'Fully connected network' between z and w
Horizontal bus line from w running right along the bottom
Three upward arrows from the bus into the three linear-transform bars
Three orange linear-transform bars 2×1×512 labelled 'Linear transform 2×1×512'
Style labels 'Style, y1', 'Style, y2', 'Style, y3' above each bar
Three upward arrows from style bars into the AdaIN slabs
Caption 'Per-channel scale and offset' beside first style arrow

interactions.label: Trace the signal
interactions.teaches: that style is a single latent w broadcast through three affine transforms into per-block scale/offset, while the constant input — not z — is what actually flows through the convolutional trunk

interactions.label: Noise scale ψ
interactions.teaches: that ψ only rescales the per-resolution noise maps z⊗ψ, so it changes stochastic detail magnitude at each scale without touching the style path; at ψ=0 the noise slabs go inert

interactions.label: Play data flow
interactions.teaches: the simultaneous timing of the three injection paths — style from below, noise from above, features left to right
which style vector y_i and which noise map z_i⊗ψ_i belong to a given synthesis block, by isolating one resolution level from the busy diagram

demo_steps.title: Mapping network
demo_steps.narration: The latent z (1×1×512) passes through the fully connected network to give the intermediate variable w (1×1×512). Nothing in the image trunk has moved yet.

demo_steps.title: One w, three styles
demo_steps.narration: w fans out along the bottom bus into three separate linear transforms, each producing a 2×1×512 style vector y₁, y₂, y₃ — one scale and one offset per channel.

demo_steps.title: Style modulates 4×4
demo_steps.narration: y₁ rises into the dark AdaIN slab and rescales every channel of the learned 4×4×512 constant. Global appearance is set here, not by any pixel-level input.

demo_steps.title: Noise injected at 4×4
demo_steps.narration: A single 4×4×1 noise map z₁, scaled by ψ₁, is broadcast to all 512 channels of the cyan slab — the same random field added to every channel.

demo_steps.title: Up to 8×8
demo_steps.narration: The block doubles in spatial resolution to 8×8×512, so the matching noise map becomes 8×8×1 while the style vector stays 2×1×512.

demo_steps.title: Turn the noise off
demo_steps.narration: Drop ψ to zero: the noise planes collapse and only the style path drives the network — the coarse content survives, the fine stochastic detail disappears.

demo_steps.title: Crank the noise up
demo_steps.narration: At ψ = 2 the noise planes and the cyan slabs they feed light up strongly; stochastic variation dominates the final 8×8×512 features and the output image.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes:
Oblique projection: each block's front face is drawn true (upright rectangle) with depth receding along +Z toward upper-right. World span roughly X ∈ [-11, 11], Y ∈ [-8, 7]. THREE ROWS, all sharing the same X axis:
• MAIN PIPELINE row centred at Y = 0, occupying X from -5.5 to +10.5, left-to-right order: grey constant block (X-width 4.0 for 512 channels × Y-height 2.2 for 4 spatial × Z-depth 1.7), thin cyan rounded slab (0.28 × 2.2 × 1.7) at x≈-1.1, thin dark-slate rounded slab (0.28 × 2.2 × 1.7) at x≈-0.65, orange 4×4×512 block (3.6 × 2.2 × 1.7) at x≈0.2..3.8, cyan slab + dark slab at x≈4.1 and 4.55, large orange 8×8×512 block (4.2 × 3.6 × 2.8) at x≈5.0..9.2 — NOTE its Y-height is 3.6 (8 spatial) vs 2.2 for the 4×4 blocks while X-width stays ~4 because both are 512 channels — tall cyan slab + tall dark slab (0.32 × 3.6 × 2.8), final orange 8×8×512 block identical in size to the previous one, then a flat pixelated output image plane (0.1 × 3.2 × 2.6) of ~8×8 brown/tan/cream squares at far right.
• NOISE row: three thin near-flat cyan parallelogram planes with only Y and Z extent (thickness ≈0.08), floating at Y ≈ +4.5, centred in X directly ABOVE the cyan slab they feed: plane 1 (4×4×1, Y-height 1.6) above x≈-1.1, plane 2 (4×4×1, Y-height 1.6) above x≈4.1, plane 3 (8×8×1, Y-height 3.2, sits higher at Y ≈ +5.2) above x≈6.9. Pale blue-grey arrows (#9fb7c4) point straight DOWN from each plane into its cyan slab.
• STYLE row: at Y ≈ -6.4, blue-grey latent bar z (2.1 × 0.30 × 0.55, #9bb6c8) at x≈-9.5 and orange bar w (2.1 × 0.30 × 0.55) at x≈-6.6, joined by a short black arrow labelled 'Fully connected network'. A single horizontal slate line runs from w rightwards at Y ≈ -6.6 to x≈8, with three upward arrows at x≈-1.1, 4.1 and 6.9 feeding three identical orange linear-transform bars (2.4 × 0.34 × 0.6) at Y ≈ -4.6. From each bar an upward slate arrow (#4c6d84) runs to Y ≈ 0 into the corresponding DARK-SLATE AdaIN slab (not the cyan one).
Palette: orange blocks #cf8066 with darker right face #a85c45 and top #e09a80; grey block #c3ccd2 / dark side #4b5b64; cyan slabs and noise planes #a8ddd2 with #2b2b2b outline; dark-slate AdaIN slabs #3f6480; arrows and bus #4c6d84; noise arrows #a9c0cc; all outlines thin black. Labels in serif math style above/below their objects exactly as in the source.
Noise magnitude rule: the displayed noise map amplitude and the cyan slab's highlight intensity scale linearly with ψ (opacity = clamp(0.15 + 0.42·ψ, 0, 1)); ψ=0 renders the noise planes nearly transparent and greys out the cyan slabs. Style path is unaffected by ψ.
interactionPlan.notes: Build with an OrthographicCamera and a fixed oblique (cabinet) shear: render each box as an extruded true-front rectangle plus two shear-offset faces (offset = 0.5·depth at 45°), or shear the projection matrix so no perspective convergence appears. Rounded slabs: RoundedBox/ExtrudeGeometry on a capsule-ish rounded-rect profile. Use EdgesGeometry + LineSegments (black, ~1.2px) on every solid for the line-art look; MeshBasicMaterial with three flat face tints (front/top/side) instead of lighting, to match the flat vector shading. Arrows as thin cylinders + cone heads in the screen plane. Labels via CSS2DRenderer/HTML overlays with KaTeX-style serif text so shape annotations stay crisp and upright. Animation: emit a glowing sphere/disc travelling along a CatmullRom path per branch (z→w, w→bus→transforms→AdaIN slabs, noise plane→cyan slab), with the pipelineStage state machine driving which paths are lit and dimming everything else to ~25% opacity. psi slider drives noise-plane opacity, a per-pixel jitter texture amplitude on the noise planes, and an emissive tint pulse on the three cyan slabs. Click picking via Raycaster on the four main blocks; selecting one dims all elements except that block, its AdaIN slab + style bar + style arrow, and its noise plane + noise arrow. Render the output image plane as a small CanvasTexture of an 8×8 grid of brown/tan values, refreshed when psi changes to hint at stochastic detail.

discrepancies: The three noise maps render as pale, almost white textured planes at ψ=1 (opacity ≈0.57 plus a near-white colour ramp), whereas the source shows solid saturated teal parallelograms — the most visible colour mismatch in the figure.

The cyan noise slabs and dark AdaIN slabs are much thinner and pressed flush against the neighbouring blocks; in the source they are distinctly separated rounded slabs with clear gaps, making the 'noise + style injection' pair readable at a glance.

Label placement collides in places: the '4×4×512' caption for the grey block sits on top of the 'Noise added to every channel' text, and the 'Linear transform 2 × 1 × 512' captions are crossed by the style arrows, unlike the clean spacing in the source.

The output RGB image is drawn as a thin box abutting the last orange block rather than the clearly detached, slightly offset pixelated face image seen at the right edge of the source; it is also noticeably smaller relative to the final block.

Overall label type size is small relative to the figure (13px body, 17px row names) compared to the source where the row labels 'Noise / Main generative pipeline / Style' and the tensor shapes are prominent typographic elements.
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-structured oblique reconstruction of the StyleGAN generator diagram with correct block hierarchy, braces, style bus and rich, conceptually meaningful interactions (stage tracing, ψ slider, block focus, guided demo); main weaknesses are washed-out noise-map colours, over-thin AdaIN/noise slabs and a few overlapping/undersized captions.
action_items: Raise the base opacity and saturation of the noise map planes so they read as solid teal like the source, reserving transparency changes for low ψ values only.
Thicken the cyan and dark-blue slabs and add a small x-gap between them and the adjacent orange/grey blocks so the noise+AdaIN pair is visually distinct as in the original.

Reposition the '4×4×512' captions and the 'Noise added to every channel' / 'Per-channel scale and offset' texts so they no longer overlap, and nudge 'Linear transform 2 × 1 × 512' clear of the style arrows.

Detach and enlarge the output RGB image plane to the right of the final 8×8×512 block, matching the offset pixelated face panel in the source, and increase overall label font sizes with a clearer hierarchy for the three row names.

feedback.rationale: The conceptual decomposition and interaction structure are correct (concept accuracy 5, no plan action items); the issues are purely implementation-level — washed-out colors, thin slabs, overlapping labels, and an undersized output plane.

demo_steps.title: Mapping network

demo_steps.title: One w, three styles

demo_steps.title: Style modulates 4×4

demo_steps.title: Noise injected at 4×4

demo_steps.title: Up to 8×8

demo_steps.title: Turn the noise off

demo_steps.title: Crank the noise up

discrepancies: Style-path arrows are drawn as long vertical shafts that pass straight through the 'Linear transform 2 × 1 × 512' and 'Style, y' captions, whereas in the source the arrow starts above the bar and the text sits clear of it — causing local clutter around all three style columns.

The two 8×8×512 volumes are only modestly larger than the 4×4×512 blocks; in the source the resolution doubling is visually dramatic (roughly double height and depth, bottom-aligned with a tall silhouette), so the key 'resolution doubles' cue is weakened.

The 'Noise added to every channel' caption is placed to the left of the first noise arrow and drifts over the grey constant block, instead of sitting to the right of the arrow as in the source; 'Per-channel scale and offset' is likewise shifted left of its arrow.

The output RGB plate is rendered as a thin slab butted against the last block rather than the detached, slightly offset parallelogram image at the far right of the source, and it lacks the distinct dark outline/perspective offset of the original.
Overall composition is rendered small in the upper-left of the canvas with a large empty band below the Style row, so proportions between the three braced rows are more compressed than in the source.
claude-opus-5.notes: A close and well-organised reproduction of the StyleGAN generator diagram with correct oblique block projection, matching palette, all three braced rows, and a rich set of genuinely pedagogical interactions (stage trace, ψ slider, flow animation, block focus, guided demo); weaknesses are minor label/arrow collisions in the style row, an understated 4×4→8×8 size jump, and a compressed layout with unused canvas space.
